Feature

How a team changed the way it works, and what happened next

A long read opens with a lead paragraph. It says what the piece is about and why a reader should stay with it.

Published
January 15
Author
The editor
Reading time
6 minutes
Topics
Topic one, topic two

The problem

The first section sets out the problem. Its paragraphs run at the text measure, so a reader never loses the line, and the sentences stay short enough to scan.

A second paragraph adds the numbers that matter. A figure such as 40 percent reads the same in any theme, because the type carries it.

What changed

The middle of the piece says what the team did, in the order it happened. Each step is one sentence: what they tried, what it cost, and what they learned from it. A reader who skims the first line of each paragraph should still follow the story.

The small steps

  • A first step, named in a few words
  • A second step, a little longer than the first one
  • A third step
  • A fourth step that shows how a list item wraps at a narrow width

What comes next

The last section says what happens now and where to read more. It ends the piece without a summary, because the lead already said what the piece is about.
